brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Provides tidy organized storage for small sewing supplies (buttons, thread, notions etc.)
requirements.evidence: Build has 3 bins on 4 hex bases: bin:-1,1,0~hex-bin-full (large open tray for tape measure/tweezer analogues), bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments holding prop:6 heap-screws-div3, prop:7 heap-nuts-div3, prop:4/9 tweezers as small-notions proxies), and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments with prop:1 marker and prop:5 solder-reel/ prop:10 brush). Compartments keep items separated; props demonstrate use. Exact sewing-specific props (thread spools, scissors, buttons) do not exist in catalog, so represented with workshop proxies.

requirements.requirement: Multiple compartments to separate different types of supplies
requirements.evidence: Two divided bins provided: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 gives 3 compartments (sockets f19-f21) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 gives 2 compartments (f22-f23), total 5 divided compartments plus 1 large open bin. Demonstrated with 5 small props seated in separate compartments.

requirements.requirement: Usable as a compact desktop organizer with a flat work surface
requirements.evidence: Cover:1,0,0;full;top creates flat deck (surface f24/f25) at story-top height 80-89mm with ruler prop:2 on it, serving as cutting/measuring surface. 4-cell footprint (~300x290mm) fits desktop. Caps installed and joints locked (14 caps, 5 jointBolts), meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Compact 4-cell sewing caddy with 3 bins (5 divided compartments + 1 open tray) and a flat cover deck. Bins staged with proxie props for small notions (screws/nuts/tweezers/solder-reel/marker/tape) to show separation; top deck holds steel rule for measuring/cutting. No new parts added in final turn per instruction. Checks pass.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
